text: This story is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-027: the matching engine, the row order, the exception list, JOB-07, the proceeds row and the ten legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC10 stay with RWB-P8-E2027-APP and RWB-P8-E2027-CON, and this story writes seven new criteria that test only the treatment-side consequence of a match.
why: The legacy key is split across rwb-payment and rwb-treatment, and the same ten criteria cannot be owned twice; the work package carries the legacy key as Split (rework) with an empty acs list for this story.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-027 sections 1 to 19, its section 12 published interfaces and its section 13 package recovery/payments/matching; Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 and R7.2 and the work package B-S2-06 story line for RWB-S2-E2027-APP.
confirm: The P8 slice owner confirms that RWB-P8-E2027-APP carries the ten legacy criteria and the matching engine.
impact: Low: the split follows the ownership map (proceeds is P8) and the work package.

text: The legacy in-process call TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid becomes one REST operation consumed from RWB-P8-E2027-CON, one hop with a 2 s timeout, called against the contract mock on Day 1; its operation name, its path detail and its payload element names are Not specified in the source documents and are taken from the baseline.
why: No source names the operation or the payload of the matching read that crosses the boundary, and the decoupling table requires a REST contract with a mock rather than an in-process call.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-027 section 12 (published interfaces) and section 13 (component list); Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-11 and ADR-020; Architecture v5 slide 17 rwb-payment contract line.
confirm: RWB-P8-E2027-CON publishes the operation, the payload and the fake before the first contract test.
impact: Medium: the client and its fake are built against a baseline that may change its element names.

text: No personal data is written, logged or put on an event by this story: the event, the record, the row and the log lines carry the case ID, the treatment ID, the payment and account codes, the rule ID, the package version, amounts and dates only, and a property check fails the build if a personal field appears.
why: The guardrails of the Template and Rules section 17 and the legacy story's own guardrail forbid personal data in events, workflow inputs and logs, and this story has no field that needs one.
read: Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 section R7.2 (s17 Guardrails); legacy RWB-E2-027 section 17 (guardrails); Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data).
confirm: The privacy owner confirms the field set of the closure event.
impact: Low: the payload is narrower than the sources allow.

text: The outbox, inbox, idempotency, decision-record, parameters, reference-data, topic-naming, Flyway and composite-route libraries, and the workflow kit, are platform wave-0 and shared-library deliverables that the service template already carries: they stand in no build row of this story, the metadata keeps Depends on (build) None, and the story builds against their fakes until they publish.
why: The pattern table adds H rows for DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 while the work package's build list is empty, and every one of those rows is a platform library or a contract the template carries.
read: Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5, R5.7 and R7.1; Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries); work package B-S2-06 story line for RWB-S2-E2027-APP (H empty).
confirm: The platform template owner confirms the library delivery date ahead of wave 2.
impact: Medium: a late library delays the story, but no H row is invented in its build list.

text: The closed plan reaches SCR-14 through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with the treatment read of this service, one hop each, read only; the route specification, the screen field list and the layout belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owners.
why: DP-19 replaces the monolith screen with a composite route, and no source publishes the route or the field list of SCR-14 in this wave.
read: Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff, one hop, 2 s, breaker per service); legacy RWB-E2-027 section 15 (screens) and the treatment screens of the sibling stories.
confirm: RWB-PLT-N001-CON publishes the SCR-14 route and its merge order.
impact: Low: the read model is proved against the route fake and switched on with the screen.

text: The DP-04 rows H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON are platform wave-0 and rwb-decision deliverables: the embedded Drools kit is the service template's own capability and the rule registry is delivered ahead of the services that evaluate its packages, so this work package does not add them to this story's build list and Depends on (build) stays None.
why: The pattern table gives DP-04 two dependencies, while the work package's build list is empty and the Drools kit is named as template wiring rather than a story of its own.
read: Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-04 and section R5.7; Temporal and Drools Design slide 11 (KIE libraries only, no KIE Server, no Business Central, no KJAR) and slide 15 (governance central in rwb-decision); Architecture v5 slide 20.
confirm: The platform and rwb-decision owners confirm the kit and the registry contract are in place before wave 2 build.
impact: Medium: the story cannot evaluate a package until the kit is wired, but no build row is invented.

text: The breach decision is taken from the package version the legacy key names, with the breach threshold read from the fired row's outputs, and this story publishes rwb.treatment.TreatmentClosed.v1 once for a breached plan; the closure of a plan that completes its own schedule stays with the plan and closure stories of the epic.
why: The legacy story owns PAYMENT_MATCH and its evaluation, the design puts the plan-breach rows under RESTRUCTURE on the treatment side, and the sibling stories of the epic leave the TreatmentClosed event to the closure story, so one reading has to be chosen for this slice.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-027 sections 2, 8 (BR10) and 13; Temporal and Drools Design slides 15 and 18; TSD S2 T4 (R-RES-25, R-RES-27, R-RES-30, R-RES-31); Architecture v5 slides 18 and 43 (TreatmentClosed); sibling stories RWB-S2-E3001-APP section 19 and RWB-S2-E3004-APP section 12.3.
confirm: The rwb-decision owner confirms which package version carries the plan-breach rows and the epic owner confirms this story owns the breached-plan closure.
impact: Medium: a wrong split would publish the event from two stories, so the once-only rule is stated in the criteria and the guard.
